change_summary: The journal retracted the paper. An institutional investigation found the data in Figures 2 to 4 had been fabricated, and the conclusions cannot be relied on. The paper's Results say Figures 2 to 4 show accuracy by dose, with 200 mg caffeine improving n-back accuracy by 12% compared with placebo, so the retraction affects the whole paper and its findings cannot be relied on.
evaluation: Your Introduction cites Brown and Kim [3] for the finding that 200 mg of caffeine improves working memory by 12%, and says this is why you chose a 200 mg dose. The paper reports that 12% improvement in n-back accuracy with Figures 2 to 4 showing accuracy by dose, and the notice says the data in those figures were fabricated and the conclusions cannot be relied on. So the retraction touches your use of this paper. The impact on you is high, because your dose rationale rests on that finding.
recommendation: Your Introduction cites Brown and Kim [3] for the finding that 200 mg of caffeine improves working memory by 12%, and says this is why you chose a 200 mg dose. The journal retracted the paper, and the notice says an institutional investigation found the data in Figures 2 to 4 had been fabricated and the conclusions cannot be relied on. Remove or replace that citation, and re-check your reasoning for the 200 mg dose using other, non-retracted evidence. Raise the dose choice with your co-authors or supervisor, and cite the retraction notice if you mention the paper.
